question: How fast can floors be replaced between guest bookings?
title: How Fast Can Floors Be Replaced Between Bookings?
h1: How Fast Can You Replace Floors Between Guest Bookings?
description: A two-person crew installs 1,000 sq ft of click LVP in 1-2 days, fitting most short-term rental gaps. Tile needs 24-72 hours of cure time after grout.
capsule: A two-person crew installs about 1,000 square feet of click LVP in one to two days on a flat, prepped slab, which fits inside most short-term rental gaps. Tile needs 24 hours before grouting and up to 72 hours before heavy furniture returns, so it rarely fits a same-week turnaround without blocking extra booking days.

sections.h2: What Fits in a Typical Booking Gap
sections.html:
A two-person crew can lay about 1,000 square feet of click-together LVP in one to two days on a slab that's already flat and prepped. Most short-term rental units are smaller than that, so a single-bedroom or condo unit often finishes faster, which is why LVP is the material most owners lean on when a floor needs to be done between two confirmed bookings.

That math changes for larger vacation homes with several bedrooms, where total square footage can push past what a single two-person crew finishes in a short gap. For those properties, we can bring in a second crew for the turnaround specifically, rather than asking one team to cover triple the usual daily pace. We'll ask about your unit's total square footage and typical booking-gap length at the estimate, since that combination is what actually determines whether a one-day or two-day install is realistic.

sections.h2: Why Tile Needs a Longer Block on the Calendar
sections.html:
Tile can be grouted about 24 hours after setting, then needs another 24 hours before regular foot traffic and 72 hours before furniture or appliances go back, according to MAPEI's installation guidance. Rapid-set products can shave time off that window, but tile still asks for more lead time than a click LVP floor does, which matters when every blocked day is a lost booking.

Bathrooms and kitchens are usually the rooms owners want in tile for durability and water resistance, and they're also the rooms where a delayed cure time matters least, since guests spend less continuous time there than in a bedroom or living room. Sequencing tile work in those spaces first, while LVP goes into bedrooms and living areas, is one way to keep a mixed-material property on schedule. We plan that sequencing out loud with you during the estimate, not after the crew has already started, so you know exactly which rooms come back online first.

Rigid-core product lines generally don't require an acclimation period before install, unlike solid hardwood, as long as the room is kept between 55-85 degrees Fahrenheit and a 1/4 inch expansion gap is left at the walls. That's one less delay to plan around when you're working against a tight turnaround.

Trim and transition strips are the detail that often gets rushed on a tight turnaround, and rushing them is a mistake. A transition strip that lifts after a week of guest traffic turns into a tripping hazard and a bad review, so we don't skip that step even when the calendar is tight. It adds minutes, not days, but it's the difference between a floor that looks finished on day one and one that starts complaining by the second guest.

sections.h2: How We Schedule Around Your Booking Calendar
sections.html:
We build the quote as a written, line-itemized document so you know exactly what's happening each day, and we can phase multi-unit properties one at a time so you're never blocking every unit's calendar for the same week. Bring your booking gaps to a free in-home estimate and we'll tell you honestly whether the timeline you're hoping for is realistic.

For properties on Siesta Key or Anna Maria Island, we also factor in typical guest check-in and check-out times when scheduling, since a crew working past a normal checkout window can create a conflict with cleaning teams arriving to reset the unit. That predictability matters more for a rental than for an owner-occupied home, where a day or two of flexibility rarely costs anyone money.

faqs.q: Does LVP need to acclimate before a fast turnaround?
faqs.a: Most rigid-core product lines don't require an acclimation period, as long as the room stays between 55-85 degrees Fahrenheit during installation and a 1/4 inch expansion gap is left at the walls.

faqs.q: Can you work while guests are checking in and out of neighboring units?
faqs.a: In a multi-unit building we typically schedule the work to avoid overlapping with active check-ins nearby, and we'll coordinate timing with your property manager if that's part of the job.

faqs.q: What's the fastest option if I only have a two-day gap?
faqs.a: Click LVP on a slab that's already flat and prepped is the most realistic option for a two-day window; tile's cure times generally don't fit that timeline.
